children: Harvey Norman gets a new bear on the furniture and homeware retailer's exposure to Australia's faltering housing market. Lowering his recommendation to underweight from neutral, Jarden analyst Ben Gilbert sees significant near-term risk for a company whose demand is supported by cohorts including home buyers. Gilbert writes in a note that he is positive on the medium-term outlook for consumer electronics--another of Harvey Norman's key product categories--but recommends that investors start buying discretionary stocks only once a stock has experienced its last downgrade. This isn't that, he reckons. Jarden lowers its target price by 16% to 3.80 Australian dollars. Shares are down 2.3% at A$4.035. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
